audit_findings.title: Parent earnings are mixed with consolidated MonotaRO cash-flow adjustments
audit_findings.magnitude: 2025 NCI earnings of $102 million, equal to 8.4% of the $1,220.8 million anchor; NCI equity of $405 million; exact OE distortion unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Parent-attributable earnings are combined with consolidated depreciation, capex, working-capital movements and potentially cash, so OE and the bridge do not represent one consistent ownership claim.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company has a controlling ownership interest in MonotaRO, the endless assortment business in Japan, with the residual representing the noncontrolling interest.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates a material outside claim on MonotaRO, while the supplied construction indicates inconsistent attribution. Because the affected business produced $102 million of NCI earnings and is undertaking expansion spending, the mismatch is reasonably capable of materially changing owner earnings. Its net direction cannot be determined without the MonotaRO adjustment components.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild each historical OE year using parent-attributable MonotaRO D&A, maintenance capex, working capital and cash; alternatively use consolidated OE and deduct the complete NCI claim, then rerun all scenarios without changing the valuation assumptions.

audit_findings.title: The null perimeter ignores the completed U.K. exit
audit_findings.magnitude: 2025 Other revenue of $324 million was 1.8% of $17,942 million consolidated sales; the first-half 2026 divestiture adjustment represented 2.3 percentage points of total-company daily-sales growth; OE effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The FY2025 anchor includes Cromwell and Zoro U.K. operations that are absent from forecast-period OE and growth.
audit_findings.evidence: Accordingly, the Company's Consolidated Statements of Earnings, Comprehensive Earnings, and Cash Flows and related notes include financial results through the divestiture date.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter mismatch is demonstrated, but the filed scale is small: Other represented 1.8% of 2025 sales, and the combined exited businesses produced a 2.3-percentage-point comparative sales adjustment in first-half 2026. Grainger also stated that the U.K. exit was not expected to materially affect future results. The recurring cash contribution remains unquantified and could have either sign, but the available scale does not reasonably threaten the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Calculate continuing-perimeter FY2025 OE excluding Cromwell and Zoro U.K. revenue, operating costs, working capital, capex, proceeds, disposal effects and closure costs; document the resulting anchor difference.

audit_findings.title: A nonrecurring, largely noncash divestiture loss appears retained in the anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $196 million comprising the $186 million Cromwell loss and $10 million Zoro U.K. closure expense; 16.1% of the $1,220.8 million anchor; a full one-for-one add-back under unchanged inputs would raise bull value per share from $440.76 to approximately $509.52
audit_findings.mechanism: The charges reduce parent earnings and therefore anchor OE; they also account for $196 million, or 30.3%, of the $647.2 million reported OE decline from 2024 to 2025 that informs the growth assessment.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company recorded a loss of $ 186 million in SG&A expenses related to the sale of this business (including cumulative translation losses related to the Cromwell business in accumulated other comprehensive losses).
audit_findings.explanation: The charges and absence of a tax benefit are demonstrated by the filing, and the supplied valuation shows no separate normalization. A full add-back would not by itself close the gap to the $1,322.135 market price, but a 16.1% anchor correction materially changes the intrinsic-value estimate and weakens the evidence supporting the reported 2025 collapse.
audit_findings.action: Trace both charges through the exact OE calculation, confirm whether the $196 million cash-flow-statement add-back was already captured, remove only amounts not already reversed, and rerun the unchanged bear, base and bull cases while separately excluding recurring U.K. operations.

audit_findings.title: Capacity-expansion capex may have been treated as maintenance capex
audit_findings.magnitude: $684 million of 2025 capex, equal to 56.0% of the $1,220.8 million anchor; the all-capex upper-bound add-back under unchanged inputs would raise bull value per share to approximately $680.72; actual growth-capex portion unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Deducting expansion expenditure as maintenance capex reduces anchor OE; MonotaRO expenditure also requires allocation between Grainger and NCI.
audit_findings.evidence: The increase reflects the continued investment in U.S. and MonotaRO supply chain capacity expansion throughout 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that 2025 investing cash use reflected U.S. and MonotaRO supply-chain capacity expansion, but it does not disclose the maintenance-versus-growth split. The $684 million upper bound would increase bull value by about $239.96 per share, or 54.4%, which is material to the intrinsic-value estimate even though it would remain below the quoted market price. The error amount remains an unresolved possibility rather than a demonstrated $684 million over-deduction.
audit_findings.action: Obtain project-level 2025 capex by maintenance, replacement, capacity expansion and technology growth; allocate MonotaRO amounts to Grainger's ownership claim, then rerun OE using the supported maintenance amount only.

audit_findings.title: The stated fully diluted denominator is explicitly incomplete
audit_findings.magnitude: 116,770 filed nonvested RSUs, equal to 0.25% of the 47.251356 million denominator; option and PSU dilution unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Omitted economically dilutive awards understate the share denominator and therefore overstate value per share and the buy-below price.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company maintains stock incentive plans under which the Company may grant a variety of incentive awards to team members and executives, which include restricted stock units (RSUs), performance shares and deferred stock units.
audit_findings.explanation: The known RSU inventory alone is only about 0.25% of the stated denominator, but the complete option and performance-unit quantities and settlement assumptions are absent. Denominator incompleteness is demonstrated; materiality of the total omission cannot be established from the supplied record. Any correction would reduce value rather than reverse the existing overvaluation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the July 2026 outstanding-share count to all RSUs, PSUs, deferred units and options using the 2026 proxy and subsequent 10-Q disclosures; apply probable performance outcomes and treasury-stock treatment, then recompute every per-share value and the buy-below price.
